:::{#thm-entropy-chain-rule-n}
#### Chain rule for entropy, many variables

For [discrete random variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X_1, \ldots, X_n$
with finite entropies,

$$\entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_n} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \entropyf{X_i \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{i-1}},$$

where the term for $i = 1$ is $\entropyf{X_1}$.

:::

::: {.proof}

The proof is by [induction](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/induction.html#def-proof-by-induction) on $n$.
The claim for $n = 1$ is $\entropyf{X_1} = \entropyf{X_1}$.

Let $n \ge 2$,
and suppose the claim holds for $n - 1$ variables.
Treat $(X_1, \ldots, X_{n-1})$ as a single variable.
The chain rule for two variables (@thm-entropy-chain-rule) gives

$$\entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_n} = \entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_{n-1}} + \entropyf{X_n \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{n-1}}.$$

The induction hypothesis expands the first summand on the right:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\entropyf{X_1, \ldots, X_n}
&= \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} \entropyf{X_i \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{i-1}} + \entropyf{X_n \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{n-1}} \\
&= \sum_{i=1}^{n} \entropyf{X_i \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{i-1}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
